knowledge:
- key_parameters: MeasurementFile=Path to the file containing uncorrected measurements (csv or xls/xlsx). Required ;; ElementFile=Path to the file containing element information (natural abundance, tracer mass shift, tracer purity). Required ;; MoleculeFile=Path to the file containing molecule information (sum formulas, tracer positions). Required ;; CorrectTracerImpurity=Logical; if TRUE, corrects for isotopic impurity of the tracer substrate ;; CorrectTracerElementCore=Logical; if TRUE, considers tracer element atoms in the core molecule. Recommended to be TRUE ;; CalculateMeanEnrichment=Logical; if TRUE, calculates mean isotopic enrichment for each molecule ;; UltraHighRes=Logical; if TRUE, performs high-resolution correction (multiple-tracer experiments). Set to FALSE for normal resolution ;; DirOut=Directory path where results and log-file are written. Defaults to '.' ;; FileOut=Base name of the output files ;; FileOutFormat=Format of output files ('csv' or 'xls') ;; ReturnResultsObject=Logical; if TRUE, returns the correction results as a list in the R session ;; CorrectAlsoMonoisotopic=Logical; if TRUE, provides monoisotopic correction results in addition to total amount ;; CalculationThreshold=Threshold to stop probability calculations in normal resolution mode (default 10^-8) ;; CalculationThreshold_UHR=Threshold to stop probability calculations in high resolution mode (default 8)
- alternatives: IsoCor (Python) for MS1-data natural abundance and tracer purity correction; ICT (Perl) for MS and MS/MS-data correction; PyNAC (Python) for natural abundance correction of high-resolution data from multiple-tracer experiments (no tracer purity correction). Prefer IsoCorrectoR when needing a single tool that handles all these features, especially tracer purity correction in high-resolution data.
- when_to_use: When analyzing mass spectrometry data (MS or MS/MS) from stable isotope labeling experiments (e.g., 13C, 15N, 18O) to correct for natural isotope abundance and tracer impurity before qualitative or quantitative metabolic flux analysis.
- pitfalls: Using high-resolution mode (UltraHighRes=TRUE) on normal resolution data (or vice versa) will abort or provide wrong results. If an element is present in the molecule information file but not in the element information file, an error occurs and correction is aborted. Providing multiple tracers in normal resolution mode, or providing a neutral loss sum formula in high-resolution mode, will cause an error. Writing results to xls format requires a Perl installation (not needed for csv). The sequence of elements in high-resolution measurement names must match the sequence of tracer elements in the molecule information file sum formula (e.g., Gly_C2.N1 matches C9N1LabC2LabN1, not Gly_N1.C2).

workflows.name: stable_isotope_correction
workflows.intent: Correct mass spectrometry data from stable isotope labeling experiments for natural isotope abundance and tracer impurity.
input: MeasurementFile (csv or xls/xlsx containing uncorrected measurements)
ElementFile (csv or xls/xlsx containing element information)
MoleculeFile (csv or xls/xlsx containing molecule information)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the IsoCorrectoR package ;; 2. Call the IsoCorrection function with paths to the measurement, element, and molecule files, along with desired correction parameters ;; 3. Retrieve the returned list containing success status, results dataframes, log, and error messages (if ReturnResultsObject=TRUE)
workflows.code:
library(IsoCorrectoR)
IsoCorrection(MeasurementFile=NA, ElementFile=NA, MoleculeFile=NA, CorrectTracerImpurity=FALSE, CorrectTracerElementCore=TRUE, CalculateMeanEnrichment=TRUE, UltraHighRes=FALSE, DirOut='.', FileOut='result', FileOutFormat='csv', ReturnResultsObject=FALSE, CorrectAlsoMonoisotopic=FALSE, CalculationThreshold=10^-8, CalculationThreshold_UHR=8, verbose=FALSE, Testmode=FALSE)
